title.narrative: Stocktake Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) for Mozambique

description.narrative: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has identified the Mozambique channel region as a climate change hotspot and Mozambique the worst affected. Over the past two decades, the country experienced an increase in extreme weather events with huge socio -economic implications. These events are projected to become only more frequent and intense in the future. In 2018, the country prepared the NDC operational plan, which informed the first approach of the national NDC. This document was presented at the 2018 United Nations Climate Summit (COP), but was not formally submitted to convection. This alignment made the conclusion of the NDC conditional on the completion of the gas inventory component and mitigation measures that should have been included in the three. There could be no NDC or Biennial Update Report (BUR) without the gas inventory component completed. In its updated NDC, Mozambique commits to a series of mitigation actions that aim to achieve a reduction of greenhouse gas emissions by about 40 million tCO2 equivalent between 2020 and 2025. These estimates will be updated with the results of the Biennial Update Report to be available in 2022. Mozambique submitted its updated NDC in 2021. The updated NDC aims to reduce emissions by approximately 40 million tCO2eq from 2020 to 2025. The updated NDC covers energy, forestry, biodiversity, agriculture and fisheries, sustainable land use, waste management, industry, early warning systems, water resources and sanitation, health, social security, infrastructure, urban areas, settlements, tourism, coastal zones, communication, and education. The estimated cost of NDC implementation is approximately USD 7.58 billion for both adaptation and mitigation actions. Mozambique has initiated the process of preparing its LT -LEDS laying out the country's emission pathway up to 2050.
